title: Banana and walnut layer cake
subtitle: two layers of moist banana sponge with cream cheese frosting and walnuts
excerpt: Very ripe bananas make the best banana cake: they are sweeter, more intensely flavoured, and have a looser texture that incorporates easily into the batter. This two-layer cake uses cream cheese frosting between the layers and on top, with walnut pieces pressed into the sides. It keeps moist for three days and improves overnight.
sourceNotes: Banana cake with cream cheese frosting is a standard British home-baking recipe widely documented from the mid-twentieth century onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: A frosting made from full-fat cream cheese, butter, and icing sugar, beaten until smooth. Less sweet than pure buttercream and tangier, it is classically paired with carrot cake and banana cake.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the un-iced sponge layers wrapped in cling film. Defrost at room temperature for 2 hours before filling and frosting.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sponge can be baked 1 day ahead. The completed cake keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.

content.text: The sponge uses mashed very ripe bananas and vegetable oil rather than creamed butter, which gives a dense, moist crumb that stays soft longer than a traditional Victoria sponge. The
is tangy and less sweet than pure buttercream, which balances the sweetness of the banana. Keep it cold until the moment of spreading.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Grease and line two 20 cm round cake tins with baking parchment.

Whisk together the mashed bananas, caster sugar, vegetable oil, and eggs in a large bowl until combined. Fold in the sifted flour, bicarbonate of soda, and cinnamon until just combined, then fold in 75 g of the chopped walnuts.

Divide evenly between the two tins and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until risen and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean and the cakes spring back when pressed lightly. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese and butter together until smooth. Add the icing sugar in stages and beat until light and creamy. Refrigerate for 15 minutes until firm enough to spread.

Place one sponge on a serving plate. Spread a generous layer of frosting on top, then place the second sponge on top. Spread the remaining frosting over the top and sides. Press the remaining 25 g of chopped walnuts onto the sides and top.

attrs.problem: Sponge dense and did not rise
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-mixing once the flour is added; this develops gluten and makes the cake heavy.
attrs.fix: Fold the flour in with a large metal spoon or spatula using as few strokes as possible.

attrs.problem: Frosting is too runny to stay on the cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid using cold cream cheese straight from the fridge (lumps) or too-warm butter (collapse).
attrs.fix: Refrigerate the finished frosting for 20 minutes before spreading, and again between crumb coat and final coat if needed.
